content: Healthcare providers are advised to develop and implement standardized protocols for routine psychosocial screening. These screenings are essential to identify psychological and social factors that may interfere with effective diabetes management. Specific issues to assess include diabetes-related distress, clinical depression, anxiety disorders, and fear of hypoglycemia. It is recommended that these screenings be conducted on a regular basis. They should also include evaluations of external stressors, such as recent changes in the patient’s health status or alterations in family support systems.
